title: The Fortuneteller and the Three Customers
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0935.txt (394 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention, except where Kogoro's name is used as a plot device (the culprit impersonated him by phone to lure the victim), which is captured as an attribute/detail on the relevant edges rather than a node. case_type: murder (with a deliberate self-implicating frame-up of two innocent people as the culprit's defining trick). Old low-fidelity file (`cases/ep935_...json`) correctly identified Sazanami Ryoichi as the culprit and the financial motive -- no correction needed there. However it was missing substantial structure found on a full read: (1) the actual murder location (Shibahama Park) and murder weapon (rope) distinct from the body-dump site (Baba mansion); (2) the secretary Ogu Masaya who discovered the body and was cleared; (3) the frame-up mechanism itself -- Sazanami stole Kanawa's lighter and Endo's brooch and planted them at the two scenes, forged a note in the victim's name naming all three suspects, used his own (falsely reported stolen) car to move the body, and made an anonymous tip call in a disguised voice to steer police to the park -- all of which is how he was ultimately identified (timestamp mismatch on the forged note vs. time of death; forensic voice match on the tip call). It also wrongly implied via `was_at` that all three suspects were physically present at the mansion; only Sazanami ever visited either scene -- Kanawa and Endo were kept alibi-less at their own homes by deceptive phone calls and implicated only through planted stolen items, corrected here.

attrs.text: "I was nearly killed again. Which one of those three did it? Is it K? Is it E? Is it S?"

attrs.content: disguised-voice call reporting a suspicious figure packing something large into a car in Shibahama Park

clues.desc: Forged note is timestamped after 10PM, but the victim died by 9PM -- she couldn't have written it, so it was planted post-mortem to implicate all three suspects at once.
The anonymous tip call that led police to the real murder scene forensically voice-matches Sazanami, who could only know that location if he was the culprit.

Kanawa and Endo both concede their own choices contributed to their misfortune, while Sazanami alone still insists Sadako's advice is entirely to blame -- leaving him as the only one with an unresolved, self-justifying grudge.
